title: Netflix Sales Growth to Decline for Fourth Quarter in a Row
summary: Netflix reported earnings for the third quarter that exceeded Wall Street expectations, but forecast a fourth consecutive quarter of slowing sales growth, a projection that may amplify concerns about the performance of the world’s leading online TV network. Netflix delivered sales of $12.9 billion in the third quarter, in line with Wall Street’s expectations, and forecast sales of $13.4 billion in the year’s final three months, falling short of what analysts have predicted. The pace of growth has fallen from 17.6% in the final quarter of last year to a projection of 11.5% for this year’s fourth quarter. The company blamed its sales shortfall on the advertising business, which is on pace to deliver $300 million less than the company expected. Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Alexis Christoforous and Norah Mulinda. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Surprising Netflix Is Not Looking at Other Opportunities: Fmr. Content Director
summary: Simon Gallagher, Hanaging Director of SPG Global and a Former Netflix Content-Acquisition Director, says hiring Peter Rice signals a more commercial programming strategy. While niche titles can succeed, Gallagher argues Netflix should lean more toward broadly appealing films and shows to support growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: United Misses Estimates, Squeezed by Soaring Jet Fuel Costs

title: PGIM’s Bryan McDonnell on 2027 Real Estate Credit Market
summary: Bryan McDonnell, Head of Real Estate Credit Strategies at PGIM, says investors should adjust business models to a higher-rate environment rather than count on rates falling. He describes the market’s recent uncertainty as a gap between rate expectations and reality, with Treasury yields rising above 5% after expectations briefly converged around 4%. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russian Satellite Raises Space Warfare Fears
summary: Clayton Swope, deputy director of the CSIS Aerospace Security Project, said that we shouldn't look at movement in Space as separate from what countries do on on earth, after a Russian satellite approached an American satellite used by Ukraine. Swope said that the move should be evaluated as an 'example of Russia doing hybrid warfare zone activities that threaten US interests and European interests' and is all part of the same geopolitical problem as the Russia Ukraine war.  (Source: Bloomberg)
